focus.title: How I work

list: Availability — I design for graceful failure: timeouts, retries, and load shedding so one bad dependency doesn't take the product down.
Capacity — I measure before I guess. Load tests, queue depth, and headroom you can see.
Efficiency — I treat compute and query cost as a feature. Smaller payloads, fewer round trips, cheaper queries.

body: This site is the same idea applied to a web page: 14kb, one round trip, nothing wasted.

this-site.title: This site
body: One HTML file under 14kb gzipped, which is about what fits in a single TCP round trip. No framework, no runtime dependencies, no webfonts.
The bento is in the HTML from the first byte, so it renders before any JavaScript runs. The detail views are the only thing that needs JS.
Built with Vite, but the output is a single file. A build step fails if the page goes over budget.
